description: Child's pose for pelvic floor relaxation: how to do it, where you should feel it, common mistakes, and easier and harder versions for tight hips.
intro: Child's pose is a kneeling rest position that gently stretches your lower back and hips. It does not build strength; its value is relaxation: it gives the pelvic floor a chance to let go, which helps if yours feels tight or you clench without noticing.
feel: You should feel a mild stretch across your lower back and hips, with a soft belly and slow breathing. You should not feel pinching in your knees, neck strain or an urge to hold your breath. Self-check: as you breathe in, notice a light widening between your sit bones; as you breathe out, let it settle without squeezing.

mistakes.wrong: Forcing your hips down to your heels
mistakes.right: Stop where it feels comfortable. A pillow between hips and heels gives the same relaxation without strain.

mistakes.wrong: Tensing your belly or pelvic floor
mistakes.right: Let the floor carry your weight. Nothing needs to work here, so soften your jaw, belly and pelvic floor.
Breathe slowly into your lower back. A slightly longer exhale helps the pelvic floor release.

easier: Put a pillow under your hips or chest, or rest your forehead on stacked fists. If kneeling bothers your knees, pad them.
harder: Walk your hands to one side, then the other, for a side stretch. Hold longer with slower breathing; no squeezes.
who: Useful for people who sit or drive for hours and anyone whose pelvic floor feels tight or hard to relax after training.
skip: Modify it if you have knee pain or recent knee or hip surgery; in pregnancy, widen your knees and support your chest. If you have pelvic pain or pain with sex, a pelvic floor physiotherapist can guide you. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Is child's pose good for the pelvic floor?
faq.a: It helps with relaxation rather than strength. The position and slow breathing make it easier for the pelvic floor to let go.

faq.q: Should I do Kegels in child's pose?
faq.a: It works better as the relaxation part of your routine. If your pelvic floor tends to be tight, more squeezing is not the fix; letting it fully release is.
